name: Inca Quarry Trail to Inti Punku (Cachicata)
why: Up the Inca quarries that supplied Ollantaytambo's temple to a stone sun gate on the ridge, 1,100 m above the valley.
book: No permit system; most walkers go with a Cusco or Ollantaytambo agency with camping gear. Ask in Ollantaytambo about the community fee.
water: Little on the way: carry 3 litres; ask at the camp about water.
dangers: Altitude: from 2,800 m to nearly 4,000 m. Acclimatise in Cusco first.
Steep and loose on the climb through the quarries.
Afternoon rain and hail from November.
turnaround: Not at Choquetacarpo by 15:00 on day 1: camp lower at the quarries.

points.name: Ollantaytambo, below the temple terraces
points.note: Walk west out of town about 1.5 km and cross the Urubamba on the bridge; the path then climbs south-west into the Kachiqhata ravine.

points.name: Kachiqhata quarries
points.note: The Inca quarries of rose rhyolite that fed Ollantaytambo's temple, with abandoned 'tired stones' and old ramps.

points.name: Inti Punku of Cachicata
points.note: A stone Inca gateway on the ridge at nearly 4,000 m. Return the same way.
